label: Figure 8.3: An $8 specific tax on concert tickets (PED greater than PES)
alt: Supply and demand for concert tickets with flat demand and steep supply; an $8 tax raises the price only from $17 to $19 so producers bear most of the burden.
caption: Demand for concert tickets is relatively elastic and supply (a fixed venue) relatively inelastic. An $8 specific tax moves the equilibrium from W (P<sub>e</sub> = $17, Q<sub>e</sub> = 50) to X (P<sub>1</sub> = $19, Q<sub>1</sub> = 30). Consumers bear only $2 per ticket (P<sub>e</sub> to P<sub>1</sub>) while producers bear $6 (C = $11 to P<sub>e</sub>), so the larger share of the tax falls on producers.
